page: Vultr voc-m-1c-8gb-50s-amd is an Optimized Cloud Compute server instance. It features a single dedicated AMD EPYC physical core operating at 2.0 GHz on the x86_64 architecture, with 1 vCPU and 1 thread per core. The hardware configuration includes 8.0 GB of system memory, providing an 8.0 GB per core ratio. Local storage is provided by a 50 GB NVMe SSD, and the instance includes one complimentary public IPv4 address. No GPU accelerators are present on this system.

Benchmark results indicate strong single-core CPU performance, with a stress-ng single-core score of 2896.39 and a Geekbench single-core score of 1999.0, both placing in the top 25% of tested systems. However, multi-core and parallel processing capabilities are limited by the single-core design, resulting in poor multi-core metrics, such as a Geekbench multi-core score of 1961.0 and a Passmark CPU score of 2424.5. Memory bandwidth is a notable bottleneck, with read-only small block cached bandwidth at 130.9 GB/sec and large block uncached bandwidth at 22.42 GB/sec, both falling into the bottom 10%. Text processing and single-threaded decompression perform at average levels, while database operations and static web serving throughput are weak to poor.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, this instance offers dedicated CPU resources and a high memory-to-core ratio for entry-level workloads, avoiding the resource contention of shared-core alternatives. However, the single-core limitation and low memory bandwidth make it less efficient for memory-intensive parallel processing or high-throughput database tasks. It is best suited for lightweight single-threaded applications, basic text processing, small-scale single-threaded utility scripts, or low-traffic web serving where dedicated CPU execution is required but multi-core scaling is unnecessary.
